title: League of Legends Patch 26.23 Notes
description: Winter map returns, balance updates galore, and a little musical Mayhem.

entries.context: Team Voice Chat is coming to League this patch in North America and Oceania! It'll be enabled shortly after the patch goes live. We'll roll out to additional regions in future patches as we gain confidence in moderation capabilities and the overall quality of the experience.

changes.text: Team Voice is enabled during champion select and while in-game. Players can be in both Party & Team Voice channels simultaneously.
Team Voice is available in all queues except for Classic.

Team Voice can only be used with push-to-talk transmission. The default key for Team Voice PTT is "C", with Character Info moved to "Z" and expanding chat history moved to "Ctrl + Z". If these keys are already manually bound, they will not be overwritten, and settings will need to be configured manually.

Five voice skins powered by Voicemod are included: Markus, Bexter, Tarys, Raghul, and Jayra. Voice skins are optional modifications that change how others hear you. When enabled, they can be applied to just team voice, or both party and team voice together.
Ignore shotcalls from Raghul at your own peril.
Added noise suppression to League's voice offerings, defaulted to on.

Input gain calibration has been added to the voice option menu in the client. When testing local playback, adjust your microphone's physical position and gain until the calibration ring is inside the shaded area and glows gold. You can also sample how you will sound with voice skins!
A report option for voice comms abuse has been added to all reporting menus.
Players who are below Honor level 3 or voice restricted from a penalty will be able to join Team Voice to listen , but will not be able to speak in it.

entries.context: Sprinting down the Rift, With the full team on the way, Past those wards we fly, To make a great outplay—Yay! Jungle's smiting creeps, Wait that's my cannon, Time to open chat, "Can we FF15?"—AFK! It's winter in the northern hemisphere (though it sure doesn't feel like it in LA) and that means the Winter Map's back, y'all! To celebrate the return of the Winter Map, all winter legacy skins will be purchasable in the Shop once patch 26.23 goes live. Those skins will remain in the Shop through the Winter Map being on early next year, so grab ‘em while you can! We'll also have a new batch of winter-themed skins coming in Patch 26.24, in case you want a little more festivity.

entries.name: Annie
entries.context: Annie has been underperforming a bit for a while now for the average player, so we're looking to give a little more fire-power and also help support her burning Tibbers build.

changes.label: Tibbers Aura Damage per Second

changes.label: Tibbers Attack Damage

entries.name: Azir
entries.context: Hello again, bird gang. We've been keeping an eye on Azir's performance as he shifts from PTA to Lethal Tempo usage. His buffs from 26.21 landed a little lower than expected, so we're giving him a little more love. Note that the attack range increase does not impact his attack range with soldiers—only when he's stuck with his own basic attacks!

changes.text: Attack Range: 525 ⇒ 550
changes.label: Attack Range

changes.text: On Hit / Attack Damage Ratio: 50% ⇒ 67%
changes.label: On Hit / Attack Damage Ratio

entries.name: Bard
entries.context: Bard has been in a pretty weak state after pro focused nerfs earlier this year, and has stopped building AP entirely. So, we're giving him a little boost to his Q base damage and ratio.

entries.name: Ezreal
entries.context: Ezreal has been underperforming at most ranks this entire year, despite still being very meta in pro play. Now that we are in the post pro play season, we're giving him a few buffs to help him succeed more in your games at home.

entries.name: Galio
entries.context: Galio's been a bit weak lately, and we want to take the time to buff him, especially to help out his weaker AP bruiser-y builds rather than only helping his current heavy AP one.

changes.text: Shield Amount (Also affects R): 7.5 / 9 / 10.5 / 12 / 13.5% of his Max HP ⇒ 8 / 11 / 14 / 17 / 20% of his Max HP
changes.label: Shield Amount (Also affects R)

entries.name: Gnar
entries.context: Like Ezreal, Gnar may be a top pick for pros, but he hasn't been performing as well in the rest of skill brackets, so we're giving his throwing arm a buff to give him a helping hand.

entries.name: K'Sante
entries.context: K'Sante is another staple in pro play at Worlds, but he isn't nearly as performant for everyone else, especially in late game where he falls off a cliff unlike most tanks.

changes.text: All Out Charge Time Damage Increase: 10 / 27.5 / 45 / 62.5 / 80% damage ⇒ 10 / 26.25 / 42.5 / 58.75 / 75% damage
changes.label: All Out Charge Time Damage Increase

entries.name: LeBlanc
entries.context: LeBlanc's damage is sitting a little too high, especially on her very dependable Q, so we're tamping down her scaling ratio to make her less oppressive, especially when snowballing.

changes.text: Ability Power Ratio (Both Initial and Mark): 40% AP ⇒ 35% AP
changes.label: Ability Power Ratio (Both Initial and Mark)

entries.name: Master Yi
entries.context: We've been keeping an eye on Master Yi for a few patches as the buffs, his Q Cooldown Refund, QoL adjustments, and jungle meta changes have settled. We think he's still a bit strong, and are tapping him down in a way that should mostly impact his crit build which has become his dominant play style, rather than his on-hit.

changes.text: Maximum Single Target Damage: 35 / 70 / 105 / 140 / 175 (+122.5% AD) ⇒ 35 / 70 / 105 / 140 / 175 (+105% AD). Reminder that this can also Critically Strike for bonus damage.
changes.label: Maximum Single Target Damage
changes.after: 35 / 70 / 105 / 140 / 175 (+105% AD). Reminder that this can also Critically Strike for bonus damage.

entries.name: Mel
entries.context: Mel's rework has landed directionally as we hoped as a moderate buff without affecting her ban rate. She's still a bit weaker than a standard champion and could use a little more firepower, so we're giving a little more strength to her Q and W.

entries.name: Syndra
entries.context: Syndra's stun feels a bit too available, so we're making it both more costly and higher cooldown early. These changes are also designed to make sure we're not pushing her into further reliance on high haste builds, and curb the ability to avoid mana investment.

changes.text: Mana Cost: 50 ⇒ 60
changes.label: Mana Cost

entries.name: Vel'Koz
entries.context: We made a small error in Vel'Koz's math. He is very displeased with us. This won't have any realistic impact on his power level.

entries.name: Vi
entries.context: Now that the pro season is over, we want to give Vi a little more strength to boost her numbers in the rest of the ladder.

entries.name: Voltaic Cyclosword
entries.context: Voltaic has been a bit too dominant as both an all-in and a poke lethality item. All-inning power is of higher importance to assassin functionality than the raw poke it's providing, so we're tuning down its trigger damage.

changes.text: Bonus Damage: [9% || 7%] target's current hp ⇒ [8% || 6%] target's current hp
changes.label: Bonus Damage

entries.name: - Urgot
entries.context: Urgot initially existed in this form from 2010-2017. Did you know that in the long past, there was an English-language community post talking about the future Urgot rework and mentioned a "Light" and "Dark" form as well as "Shotgun knees." I'm pretty sure that's why the 2017 Urgot rework has shotgun knees, but who's to say? He's somewhat of an AD juggernaut. Manamune is very useful, as are tanky items like Frozen Heart, since his ultimate will place him right inside of the enemy team comp. Please don't swap in the enemy Alistar; it might lose you a game at WCG 2010.

entries.context: We're back with more content and balance changes for ARAM Mayhem! Four new Headliners are hitting the stage, bringing new ways to play. Whether you're looking for a second chance at life with Arcade, protecting your team with La Ilusion, getting rich with Debonair, or finding the perfect Augment with Maestro, we're excited for you to enjoy the show. We've also been keeping an eye on how the new set is playing out and listening to your feedback. Turrets have been falling a little too quickly, barely slowing down enemies and buying little-to-no time for their teams. We're experimenting with turret playing and increasing their defenses so games don't end in a blink. Tanks have had a particularly tough time keeping up with the chaos, so we're introducing four new tank-focused Augments to help our beefier champions stay in the fight. We're also making another round of champion balance adjustments to give some struggling picks a helping hand while bringing down a few overperformers. Finally, we're dialing back Bouncing Bees and Boom and the Bass, which have been putting out a little more damage than we'd like. As always, thank you for playing and keep the feedback coming!

entries.name: Turret Plating
entries.context: Turrets in Mayhem now have 120 Armor and 120 Magic Resistance, and no longer have their resists lowered as the game goes on. Outer and inhibitor Mayhem turrets now have Turret Plating. Plating separates the health bar into thirds, with destroyed plates giving 100g split among the team nearby. On plate destruction, the tower gets a Bulwark buff that grants 60-80 resists per nearby champion.

entries.context: The replay download limit has been changed from 10 per hour to 50 per day. A few patches ago we instituted a download limit on replays to prevent large-scale abuse of downloaded replays by bad actors using vibecoded apps to scrape thousands upon thousands of replays. We opted for a time-based limit to still allow creators to make content, while preventing mass exploitative downloads. In order to make replays more accessible for community members that need them while still reducing risk to game integrity, we're shifting to a daily limit.

We're updating DJ Sona's interactive music to get it more in-line with her original release. The music implementation from the original 2015 version was very resource intensive, and wasn't sustainable long-term. Which is why we released an optimization in 2018. But, since then we've made a variety of changes to how we implement music systems in League, and we've improved our optimization methods. Along with the Mythic Variant release, we're updating existing DJ Sona that, while not a 1:1 recreation of the original release, captures the intentions of the original music system. This will add the following features:

changes.text: With each use of Sona's ability, the music will respond by "unlocking" an additional layer, building towards a full track.
Upon death, these layers will reset and go away. If you fire off your abilities again, you will build the tracks back up.
Upon using your R at levels 6, 11, and 16, your music changes state to play higher intensity playlists.
The interactive layers still persist across all levels.
We've also fixed the HUD mute and unmute button behavior that had been unreliable and unresponsive to work in similar manners with any other champions with mute-able music.

entries.context: We're excited to share that this time, we're collaborating with a renowned American electronic music producer and DJ: underscores to bring Sona to the stage collaborating with True Damage, KDA, and Heartsteel.
